A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GTO research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. Appendices A–D are retained; v2 adds Appendices E–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding-efficiency experiments, compatibility evaluations, and ablations in Figure 2 and Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds Qwen3-8B results, a continued-training comparison, and tree-configuration experiments in Tables 1, 6, and 7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same tree reward, reference-model debiasing, adjacent-prefix grouping, clipped objective, and token-level loss. Appendix E evaluates the existing trained method under different inference configurations without introducing a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use ShareGPT and OpenThoughts-114k-math for training and MT-Bench, HumanEval, and GSM8K for evaluation. The additions concern target models, training controls, and tree configurations within the existing tasks, rather than new datasets or domains.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds an explicitly evaluated continued-training EAGLE-3 comparator for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B. The original comparator sets remain intact. The new Qwen3-8B comparison uses the already evaluated EAGLE-3 baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds two substantive evaluation designs: an EAGLE-3 control receiving 200 additional A100-80GB GPU-hours with the same data, and evaluation of a drafter trained at depth 7 with 60 tokens across depths {6,7,8} and token budgets {50,60,70}. It also adds Qwen3-8B. Existing metrics, batch size, and temperatures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained aggregation, group-size, and debiasing ablations, Table 6 tests whether extra training compute explains GTO's gains. Appendix E and Table 7 test sensitivity to changing inference tree configurations after training. These substantially extend the questions investigated by the supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added discussion of group-normalization variance concerns optimization, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original result entries remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results. Table 1 reports Qwen3-8B average speedups of 2.72 versus EAGLE-3's 2.50 at T=0 and 2.47 versus 2.36 at T=1. Table 6 adds continued-training averages of 3.60 and 3.13, below GTO's retained 3.89 and 3.27. Table 7 adds eight nondefault configurations alongside the retained default, with average speedups spanning 3.49–3.81 at T=0 and 2.80–2.95 at T=1.

T1.justification: The reward definitions, Theorem 1, Appendix A proof, and Appendix B loss derivation are unchanged. The new GRPO discussion and tree-compatibility explanation introduce no formal result or revised proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same misalignment diagnosis, two proposed components, theoretical guarantee, and headline acceptance-length and speedup claims. Adding Qwen3-8B to the abstract's examples supplies further support without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds focused interpretations attributing gains to the objective rather than extra training, explaining large-group weakness through normalization-induced signal attenuation, and attributing tree-configuration transfer to learned token alignment. Appendix E extends applicability claims to dynamic tree changes, although its evidence covers only nearby configurations on one target model. The original training-cost limitation remains.

D1.justification: The abstract and Appendix B newly provide a repository link described as supplying code, draft models, scripts, and additional hyperparameters. Appendix D changes the model-size category associated with 200 GPU-hours from 7B to 8B. New experiments document their control budget and configuration grid; the original default tree and optimizer settings were already disclosed.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Qwen3 technical report citation and connects the existing group-size findings more explicitly to the already cited GRPO work. The related-work section and positioning around draft-policy misalignment remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. v2 adds localized experimental discussion, Appendix E, acknowledgements, an ethics statement, and an LLM-usage statement, and updates the publication header. These are extensions rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a Qwen3-8B block, and Tables 6–7 are added using the existing table style. Figures 1–2 and Tables 2–5 retain their displays. Pagination shifts, including placing Appendix D's compute discussion together below Algorithm 1, produce limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: The continued-training control addresses a previously untested alternative explanation for GTO's gains, while Qwen3-8B results, tree sensitivity tests, and access information strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. These gains are bounded: the control covers one target model, and Appendix E's broad claims about dynamic-tree generalization exceed its nearby-configuration tests and lack configuration-matched baseline comparisons. The net improvement is useful but limited.
